components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action per viewport: tickets, booking, buy.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 2.75rem; padding: 0 1.5rem; background: #a9b98a; color: #000000; border: 0; border-radius: 2px; font-family: 'Cinzel Variable', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.9375rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1), transform 90ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #7d9160; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a9b98a; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary actions beside a primary: booking contact, more videos.

components.name: Link

narrative.overview:
A ritual held in a clearing under a black sky. The band's monochrome logo stands at the centre: void black, cool bone white, antler grey. The forest is the dark around it: pine at the edges, moss on the ground, and lichen as the pale trail that marks the way in. Warm colour stays rare. Bark and ember read as a single torch among the trees, never as the ground. The site should feel like that clearing just before the first drum hit.

The system is dark, spacious and flat. Hard, cut edges and a faint engraving grain keep the woodcut character of the band's artwork. Ceremony comes from scale, rhythm and restraint, not from added ornament, and photography, the logo and the band's own engravings carry the identity; the system frames them and never competes. Darkness must not cost speed or legibility on a phone arriving from Instagram on 4G: every texture is CSS or inline SVG, and every text pair passes WCAG 2.1 AA.

Rejected outright: warm cream-and-brown dominance and the Renaissance-fair palette (parchment, burgundy, gold, tavern browns), generic SaaS layouts, glossy gradients, neon or cyberpunk colour, and cartoon fantasy.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome logo anchors on black; forest greens as atmosphere.
One action colour (pale lichen); warm colour rationed like firelight.
Square to near-square edges (0–4px), no shadows, depth from tonal steps.
Blackletter for display only; carved roman capitals for structure; Garamond for reading.
Percussive motion: a short hit, then stillness.

rules.name: The Monochrome Anchor Rule
rules.body: Void, bone and antler grey come from the logo and are used exactly as given. Green is atmosphere around the logo, never a replacement for it.

rules.name: The Lichen Path Rule
rules.body: Lichen marks where to go: action, link and focus. At most one lichen-filled button per viewport, and lichen is never spent on decoration.

rules.name: The Torch Rule
rules.body: Bark and ember together cover less than 5% of any viewport; ember appears once or twice per page. If the page starts to look warm, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Never-Text Rule
rules.body: Shadow Moss and Antler Grey are never text colours. Wet Bark is never small text.

rules.name: The Seen-Edge Rule
rules.body: A border that must be seen (inputs, toggles, frames around controls) uses Shadow Moss on void, pine-950 or pine-900. On a pine-800 surface, use lichen or bone instead. Colour never carries meaning alone: "sold out" is written, and errors are written.

rules.name: The Blackletter Threshold Rule
rules.body: Pirata One is for h1, h2 and the hero only, and never below 28px. Body text, labels, dates and buttons are never set in blackletter.

rules.name: The Logo Is Not a Font Rule
rules.body: The wordmark is always the band's supplied artwork, never re-set in type.

rules.name: The Flat Grove Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs to stand out, give it a lighter pine surface or a Shadow Moss edge, never a shadow.

dos: Do use semantic tokens in components (`bg-bg`, `bg-surface`, `text-fg`, `text-fg-muted`, `bg-accent`, `border-border`, `ring`), never primitives or raw hex.
Do keep every text pair at WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and control edges. The full matrix is in `design-system/ritus-ferae/MASTER.md`.
Do spend Pale Lichen only on action, links and focus, with one lichen-filled button per viewport.
Do give every interactive element the 2px Pale Lichen focus ring with a 2px offset.
Do keep tap targets at least 44 × 44px with at least 8px between them.
Do let real photography, the logo and the band's engravings lead; the system only frames them.
Do check every layout at 360, 768, 1024 and 1440px in both Spanish and English (Spanish runs about 15–25% longer).
donts: Don't let warm cream or brown dominate, and don't use a Renaissance-fair palette (parchment, burgundy, gold, tavern browns).
Don't let bark and ember together exceed 5% of a viewport, or use ember more than twice on a page.
Don't use Shadow Moss or Antler Grey as text, or Wet Bark as small text.
Don't add shadows of any kind (drop, glow, coloured halo or hard offset) or `translateY` hover lifts.
Don't use pill shapes or radii above 4px.
Don't set blackletter below 28px or anywhere outside `h1`, `h2` and the hero.
Don't use glossy gradients, glassmorphism, backdrop blur, neon or cyberpunk colour, or cartoon fantasy (faux-parchment scrolls, Papyrus-style faces).
Don't use floaty motion: fades longer than 300ms, parallax, animated smoke or scroll-jacking.
Don't use emoji as icons or mix icon sets; use one stroke SVG set with `currentColor`.
Don't use placeholder-only form labels, hide focus states, or autoplay anything with sound.
